tweets.text:
In direct placement, singulated dies on a film frame get cleaned and plasma activated, then a flip chip bonder places them one at a time onto the activated target wafer.

In collective die-to-wafer, dies are picked and placed onto a reconstituted carrier wafer which is then plasma activated and fusion bonded to the target wafer in a wafer-to-wafer bonder.

The difference is where the final bond happens. Direct placement is the simpler flow, but overlay is capped by the bond head, roughly 1 µm in production. Collective moves the final bond into a W2W tool, so all dies bond in one shot with wafer-to-wafer-class throughput, at the cost of an extra carrier bond and de-bond loop. (2/2)
